events.event_hazard: Accident at TEPCO’s Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station (nuclear accident)
affected_locations: Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station (NPS), Japan
key_impacts: Accident damaged Fukushima Daiichi NPS units, leading to a mid- and long-term decommissioning of Units 1–4.

Large volumes of ALPS-treated water containing tritium and other radionuclides stored on site: about 1,100,000 m3 as of October 2018, with planned tank capacity of 1.37 million m3 expected to be reached within three to four years.

Generation of contaminated water reduced from approximately 490 m3/day (FY2015 average) to approximately 200 m3/day (first half FY2018) through measures including subdrain repair and the “frozen soil wall.”
Fuel debris deposits are present in Units 1–3; internal PCV investigations have identified deposits and support future retrieval.
Preparations to remove spent fuel from the pools are advanced for Unit 3 and progressing for Units 1 and 2.
